plan.notes: Source: Marquette University 2026-2027 Undergraduate Bulletin (official, bulletin.marquette.edu), 'Computer Science, BS' program page, 'Typical Program for Computer Science Majors' section (freshman/sophomore/junior/senior first- and second-term tables with printed semester totals). Source URL: https://bulletin.marquette.edu/arts-sciences/computer-science/computer-science-bs/computer-science-bs.pdf (official bulletin-generated PDF of the same page; 2026-2027 Bulletin confirmed as current via bulletin.marquette.edu homepage 2026-09-30). Degree name verified: 'Computer Science, BS' (bulletin heading) — credential matches target exactly, no substitution. Transcription method: manual verbatim transcription of the official term-by-term typical-program tables (course codes, titles, credit hours, printed semester totals); all course titles are the bulletin's own catalog titles (Required Computer Science Courses and Required Mathematics Cognate Courses tables on the same page), not invented. CORE 4929 title = 'The Service of Faith and Promotion of Justice' (bulletin MCC requirements); ARSC 1953 = 'Exploring Arts and Sciences' (bulletin First-Year Seminar requirement). CREDIT-TOTAL CAVEAT: total_credits=122 is the typical program's OWN printed total (16+14+16+16+15+15+15+15=122), which the bulletin states explicitly as 'Total Credit Hours: 122'. The university bachelor's minimum is 120 credits (bulletin Graduation Requirements), so the sample as printed carries 2 extra elective credits; total_credits is set to the sample's own total (122) so the pipeline's exact credit-sum check passes (Clarkson/UVM/GCSU precedent). Choice-slot modeling: official either/or requirements (MATH 2100 or 2350; COSC 3410 or COSC 4400), 'or elective' alternatives (CORE 1929, CORE 4929), 'Any 1/Any 2/Remaining 1' MCC Foundation picks, Discovery Tier (DSCV) courses, the 4-credit lab science + 3-credit science elective (footnote: 6+ hrs BIOL/CHEM/PHYS incl. lab), and the required 12 credits of upper-division COSC electives are modeled as constrained-choice slots with distinct placeholder codes. 'COSC 3xxx/4xxx' elective slots are given distinct codes (COSC-EL-1 through COSC-EL-4) since the pipeline rejects duplicate non-choice codes. The bulletin sample publishes no per-course prerequisites, so prereq arrays are left empty rather than inferred. Catalog year used: 2026-2027 (actual year of the source). Total courses: 36.

courses.title: MCC Foundation Course (any 1 of ENGL 1001, PHIL 1001, THEO 1001, ESSV1)
courses.choice_note: Student choice: any of ENGL 1001 Foundations in Rhetoric, PHIL 1001 Foundations in Philosophy, THEO 1001 Foundations in Theology: Finding God in All Things, or ESSV1 Engaging Social Systems and Values 1 (MCC Foundations tier).

courses.title: Natural Science with Laboratory (BIOL, CHEM, or PHYS with lab)
courses.choice_note: Per bulletin footnote: must complete at least 6 credit hours of Natural Science electives (BIOL, CHEM or PHYS), including at least one course with a laboratory component. The typical program places 4 credits of lab science in Fall Year 1 and 3 credits of science elective in Fall Year 3 (7 credits total).

courses.title: Discovery Tier Course (MCC) I
courses.choice_note: One of four required Discovery Tier (DSCV) MCC courses. Per bulletin: the four DSCV courses must be completed in the same theme and include Humanities (HUM), Social Science (SSC), Natural Science and Mathematics (NSM) and one elective (ELE) content areas; a maximum of two Discovery Tier courses can apply towards a primary major. The Writing Intensive (WRIT) and ESSV2 requirements can be fulfilled through designated Discovery Tier or other degree courses.
